The -ed Ending

/t//d//ɪd/
after a voiceless consonant

talked · kissed · helped
worked · checked · pushed		 after a voiced consonant or a vowel

played · closed · opened
plugged · failed · charged		 only after the sounds t or d

painted · needed
tested · connected
/t/ is voiceless. /d/ is voiced.
So each ending simply matches the sound in front of it.

1 · There is only one mistake

Do not add a syllable.
Unless the verb already ends in a t or d sound, in which case you must.

2 · The only question that matters

Say the base verb. Then say the past form. Did the -ed add a syllable?

Verb 1 of 0
·
 

3 · Same verb, both endings

Tap either form to hear the ending.

presentpastboth are
it worksit worked/s/ then /t/, voiceless
it plugsit plugged/z/ then /d/, voiced
it failsit failed/z/ then /d/, voiced
it helpsit helped/s/ then /t/, voiceless
it testsit testedthe extra syllable, both times

4 · The exceptions

Some adjectives ending in -ed ignore the rule entirely and take /ɪd/, even though no t or d comes before it.

naked /ˈneɪkɪd/   wicked /ˈwɪkɪd/   sacred /ˈseɪkrɪd/   beloved /bɪˈlʌvɪd/   rugged /ˈrʌɡɪd/

⚠ NO NAKED FLAMES

You have walked past that sign. It is NA-kid, two syllables, not naked rhyming with baked. And rugged is ordinary industrial English: a rugged enclosure, a rugged casing, said RUG-gid.

The test is grammatical, not phonetic: if it is an adjective rather than a past verb, it may take /ɪd/. Compare he learned it (verb, one syllable ending) with a learned professor (adjective, LEARN-id).

5 · Say it

The orange endings are the only ones that add a syllable. Everything else stays exactly as long as it was.

We checked the fuse, switched it off and helped the group. (three verbs, no extra syllables)
We connected the board, tested the sensor and recorded the value. (three verbs, three extra syllables)
The circuit failed, so we replaced the capacitor and restarted the system.
It worked. It worked. It worked. (one syllable, every time)
no extra syllableworked · checked · switched · helped · pushed · released · plugged · failed · charged · designed · installed · measured
extra syllabletested · connected · started · loaded · recorded · converted · mounted · welded · protected · calibrated
adjectivesnaked · wicked · sacred · beloved · rugged (all /ɪd/, all breaking the rule)
